doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Ellington reed section, Sonny Greer and music for dancing
summary: Williams praises the reed chorus on 'Cotton Tail', quotes Sonny Greer on a drummer's job, and laments the loss of ballrooms.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I love that. People talk about Ben’s solo, but one of the things that I love about it is the reed chorus.

For all the reeds. [scats] They was like swinging. [scats] And Sonny Greer, nobody talks about him, but Sonny Greer had the theory, he had the theory that he said, somebody said to him, “How, what is the job of a drummer with the band.” Sonny said, “To try not to get in the way.”
And they would swing, you know [scats]

That beat, oh it was really beautiful to watch and to listen to. My band, boy. Dancing there. Now there’s one that Ellington used to talk about. He said our music was made for dancing. But there’s no more ballrooms for us now, you know?
